<!-- All news items below this line -->{{Current events|year=2006|month=05|day=16|content=

* The United States releases a list of 759 former and current inmates of the [[Guantanamo Bay detention camp]] in [[Cuba]] after a [[Freedom of Information Act (United States)|Freedom of Information Act]] action was filed by the [[Associated Press]]. [http://www.defenselink.mil/pubs/foi/detainees/detaineesFOIArelease15May2006.pdf (Pentagon list)] [http://www.theage.com.au/news/World/US-names-759-Guantanamo-inmates/2006/05/16/1147545296196.html (The Age)]
* [[War in Darfur]]: The [[United Nations Security Council]] [[United Nations Security Council Resolution 1679|votes unanimously]] to initiate the process which would lead to a [[List of UN peacekeeping missions|UN peacekeeping force]] relieving the beleaguered [[African Union Mission in Sudan|African Union peacekeepers]] in the war-torn [[Darfur]] region of [[Sudan]]. The Government of Sudan opposes the move. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/africa/4987414.stm (BBC)], [https://web.archive.org/web/20060516233013/http://voanews.com/english/2006-05-16-voa75.cfm (VoA)]
* [[Chad]]ian Information Minister [[Hourmadji Moussa Doumgor]] accuses the Government of Sudan of facilitating a new alliance between [[Mahamat Nour]]'s [[United Front for Democratic Change|UFDC]] and the defected troops of Mahamat Nouri against the [[Idriss Déby|Déby administration]]. Neither group has confirmed or denied the merger. [http://www.cnn.com/2006/WORLD/africa/05/16/ChadSudanRebels.reut/index.html?section=cnn_latest (CNN)]
* Italian centre-left leader [[Romano Prodi]] is given the mandate to form a new government by [[President of Italy|President]] [[Giorgio Napolitano]]. Prodi is supposed to present his list of ministers on May 17. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/4987942.stm (BBC)]
* At least 23 people have been killed in a shooting and bombing attack in the [[Iraq]]i capital, [[Baghdad]], police say. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/4986868.stm (BBC)]
* [[Mark Inglis]], a New Zealander,  became the first double-amputee to climb [[Mount Everest]] [http://news.scotsman.com/latest.cfm?id=(hampton)]
* A British-Ugandan team reports a substantial reduction in [[glacier|glacial cover]] atop the [[Rwenzori Mountains]] in Central Africa, attributable to increases in air temperature over the past four decades.  This "[[Mountains of the Moon (Africa)|Mountains of the Moon]]", according to [[2nd century]] geographer [[Ptolemy]], is one of the sources of the [[Nile]], and is projected in the study to disappear in two decades. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/4987186.stm (BBC)]
* A [[tattoo]]ed [[mummy]] of a woman in her late 20s of the [[Moche culture|Moche]] tribe from 1,500 years ago is found near [[Trujillo, Peru]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/4988540.stm (BBC)]
